data.title: Bulls vs. Bears: Is CoreWeave the canary in AI coalmine?
data.description:
CoreWeave fell more than 25% this week as the data ‌center operator’s debt reached distress levels, triggering a broader sell-off in semiconductor stocks amid concerns over the massive debt-fueled expansion of the AI sector.

However, Seeking Alpha analysts had mixed views on the company throughout the week, even as its shares went on to sink more than two-thirds from a peak in June 2025, recording the worst weekly decline in nearly a year.

The Bulls

“CoreWeave has experienced a massive valuation drop this week amid heightened concerns over its debt-financed AI infrastructure buildout,” wrote analyst The Asian Investor in “CoreWeave: Why The Bond Crash Doesn't Change The Bullish Case.”  “Nvidia, owning ~10% of CRWV, could provide strategic financing support and may intervene if debt markets tighten further in my opinion.”

“At the current valuation, we believe the company offers a rare combination of value and growth elements,” added DPRG Investment Management in “CoreWeave: Asymmetric Risk-Reward As $104 Billion Backlog Underpins Growth.” “At the current valuation, we believe the company offers a rare combination of value and growth elements.”

“The recent $4.2 billion convertible bond deal significantly lowers interest costs, improving CoreWeave’s path to profitability despite potential dilution risks,” noted Rick Orford in “CoreWeave: A Number Hiding In Its Bond Paperwork Faces A Big Test By March 2027.”  “I think the stock is priced for the worries, not for what could come next, which is usually a good spot for patient investors.”

The Bears

“CRWV's contracts with hyperscalers are thin-margined or loss-making, funding infrastructure but not delivering core profitability,” added analyst Bashar Issa in “CoreWeave: It's Worse Than You Think; Take Your Money And Run (Rating Downgrade).” “Rising borrowing costs and deteriorating bond prices threaten CRWV's capital-intensive, leveraged growth model, risking a negative feedback loop.”

“Despite robust demand, CRWV’s business model relies on borrowing at rates now exceeding its rental yields, resulting in a wide negative spread,” opined Dustin Quasney in “CoreWeave: Why Credit Markets See A 54% Chance Of Default.” “CRWV shareholders face significant downside as debt outpaces asset returns; at current prices, CRWV equity is essentially a leveraged call option on both credit market recovery and sustained AI shortages.”

“CoreWeave has become dramatically cheaper, but financing is becoming more important than the backlog,” added Infinity Curve in “CoreWeave: Why I Sold Before The Next Shock.” “Demand remains strong, but $35-$39 billion of expected annual capex makes cash conversion and financing conditions increasingly critical for shareholders.”

“Despite 112% YoY revenue growth and a $104B backlog, CRWV's rising interest expense and aggressive capex outpace operating income, threatening equity value,” noted SA Investing Group Leader James Foord in “CoreWeave: AI's First Casualty.”  “CRWV's survival hinges on securing lower-cost capital or an investment-grade partner, but current conditions favor bondholders over shareholders.”

“CRWV faces a lose-lose scenario: higher debt yields erode FCF, while equity issuance causes massive dilution,” argued Cavenagh Research in “CoreWeave: The Bond Selloff May Have Broken The Equity Story.” “Reducing growth or CAPEX is not viable, as CRWV's valuation depends on aggressive expansion and operating leverage.”

data.title: Vitalik Buterin Reveals Why AI Could Push Bitcoin Miners Out
data.description:
Bitcoin mining cost is split roughly evenly between hardware and electricity, Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin said on X. AI inference, by contrast, is almost entirely a hardware bill, he added.

That contrast matters because miners and AI firms increasingly chase the same power sites. Yet the two industries spend their money in very different places.

What Drives Bitcoin Mining Cost Per Coin?

Buterin shared the observation alongside a cost table. Its line items add up to roughly $93,700 per coin.

Electricity is the largest line. Power fed directly into the machines costs $40,600 per coin, or 43.3% of the total. Other electricity adds another $2,400.

Meanwhile, compute capital expenditure (capex) runs about $37,600. That covers hardware, cooling, and power gear, including financing, and equals roughly 40% of the Bitcoin mining cost.

Labor, facility rent, maintenance, insurance, taxes, and bandwidth make up the remaining 14% or so. That leaves electricity and compute capex close to even, at roughly 46% and 40%.

The table’s total lands above JPMorgan’s recent Bitcoin production cost estimate of $85,000.

It also sits above Bitcoin’s current price, so an average miner would not cover its full costs.

Why AI Plays by Different Power Rules

AI inference flips that ratio, according to Buterin. Running trained models depends mostly on expensive chips, so power takes a much smaller slice of each dollar.

As a result, an AI operator can likely absorb higher electricity prices than a miner can. For miners, however, power makes up a far larger share of Bitcoin mining cost.

That gap already shapes the market. Many miners hold permitted grid capacity that AI developers can’t build fast enough, as local data center restrictions spread.

Some industry voices now ask whether AI could push mining out of the most expensive sites entirely.

Others want to merge the two models. BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes, for instance, is building a Bitcoin-style AI mining network that pays GPU owners.

If Buterin’s math holds, cheap power remains the miner’s edge, while cheap capital favors AI. The next contest for energy sites may hinge less on Bitcoin mining cost and more on who can finance hardware fastest.

data.title: Q2 results 2026 race: HDFC vs ICICI Bank vs Axis Bank vs Yes Bank vs IDBI - Which bank won in PAT, NII, revenue growth?
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 17 -- HDFC vs ICICI Bank vs Axis Bank vs Yes Bank: The weekend was not a busy day for investors tracking bank stocks as multiple lenders, including HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank, IDBI Bank, and Yes Bank, announced their second quarter results for the financial year 2026-27 on Saturday, October 17.

While ICICI Bank, Axis Bank, and Yes Bank reported double digit growth in net profit after tax (PAT), HDFC Bank saw single digit PAT growth in Q2FY27. Contrastingly, IDBI Bank saw 39% decline in its net profit, as its performance was overshadowed by steep high-base effect amid developments linked to privatization.

Here's a thorough comparison of ICICI, HDFC, Axis, Yes and IDBI Bank Q2 results in terms of profit, net interest income (NII) and revenue.

The private lending giant reported a 4.7% annual jump in its standalone net profit to Rs.19,510 crore for the July-September quarter of FY27. Sharp 67% decline in treasury trading gains affected HDFC Bank Q2 result. Its treasury trading gains fell to Rs.780 crore from Rs.2,390 crore in the corresponding quarter.

ICICI Bank reported a 20.1% annual jump in standalone net profit to Rs.14,843 crore in Q2FY27. The double digit growth was supported by strong loan growth and lower provisions for bad loans.

The bank's net interest income (NII), the difference between interest earned and interest paid, rose 17.7 % to Rs.25,339 crore in the July-September quarter, compared with Rs.21,529 crore in the corresponding period last year.

Axis Bank reported a 38% annual jump in its net profit to Rs.7,003 crore during the quarter under review. The sharp jump in net profit was led by decline in provisions and improving asset quality.

Its provisions and contingencies fell to Rs.1,694 crore from Rs.3,547 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

IDBI Bank reported a 39% annual decline in its net profit to Rs.2,205 crore in Q2FY27. The decline in net profit was largely due to one-time gain recorded last year. Apart from the decline in profit, IDBI Bank's underlying profit surged by 14% amid stronger interest income and improved asset quality.

Its net profit stood at Rs.3,627 crore in the corresponding quarter last year, which included a one-time gain of Rs.1,699 crore from the sale of its strategic investment in National Securities Depository Limited (NSDL).

Mumbai-based Yes Bank reported 65% annual jump in its consolidated net profit to Rs.1080 crore in Q2FY27 against Rs.654 crore in the year ago period. Its NII grew by 22.7% annually.

Based on the Q2FY27 numbers, Yes Bank has delivered the highest profit growth, IDBI and Yes Bank showcased aggressive NII expansion. Yes Bank won in terms of asset quality as it maintained lowest net NPA in the quarter.

data.title: Rubio’s Jamnagar visit may focus on Reliance’s Texas refinery deal, boost Trump’s midterm prospects: Expert
data.description:
Offering deep insights into the strategic and commercial currents shaping India-US ties, foreign affairs expert Robinder Sachdev has highlighted that the upcoming visit of US Secretary of State Marco Rubio to Jamnagar and Mumbai carries critical economic and political objectives, particularly centred on corporate investments and upcoming US midterm dynamics.

Speaking to ANI, Sachdev analysed ongoing political and corporate engagements between India and the United States, focusing specifically on the diplomatic visit.

Rubio’s Jamnagar visit may focus on Reliance’s US refinery investment

Sharing his perspective on diplomatic engagements, Sachdev discussed the significance of official visits. “I think the visit of Marco Rubio, Secretary, is definitely a good sign, a good signal in US-India relations. Apart from other things, there is one speculation I have about his visit and the objectives of his visit. I am looking into why he is going to Jamnagar. That’s an important visit,” he noted.

Detailing expectations surrounding upcoming corporate investments, he added, “In my mind, Rubio is looking to finalise the agreement which Reliance has made to invest in a refinery in the United States. A few weeks ago, Trump announced that a $300 billion project with Reliance will come up in Brownsville, Texas. That $300 billion number is a very large number. It’s not the investment into the refinery; it’s about $5 billion, whatever it may be.”

In March 2026, US President Donald Trump announced a USD 300 billion partnership with India’s Reliance Industries for the “America First Refining” project at the Port of Brownsville, Texas.

US midterm elections could shape investment announcement

Highlighting domestic political contexts in the United States, Sachdev observed, “Right now, the midterms are in full swing in America. There are about five or six Senate races where Republicans are facing a very tough challenge and, surprisingly, one of the tough Senate races is in Texas, which is typically a stronghold of Republicans.

Now, my guess or estimate is that Secretary Rubio will look to finalise this deal here so that, in three to four days, Donald Trump can, of course, claim one more investment officially by Reliance. Secondly, in the Senate race in Texas, it will give the Republican candidate some talking points to tell Texans that, look, this is what we are doing. We are bringing in a large investment from Reliance in India, and where this refinery is to be set up in Brownsville, there is a large number of Latino voters and construction labourers.”

Discussing potential political advantages, he remarked, “So, they’re looking to maybe capture that political benefit of this refinery announcement. That is my speculation as to the outcome or the key takeaway that Secretary Rubio would look to take from this visit, apart from definitely his discussions with Indian officials, Indian corporates and all.

I do not expect, I do not know what progress there can be on the US-India trade deal, but by all intents and purposes, I think this visit of Secretary Rubio is to finalise and have an official announcement from Reliance that it will be investing in this refinery in Texas, which will give Trump and the Republican Senate candidate in Texas, Paxton, talking points to claim that they are bringing investments and jobs and, therefore, they would look to get some benefits in the midterm elections from this announcement.”

Rubio and Jaishankar to discuss regional and global issues

Addressing broader diplomatic schedules and regional discussions, Sachdev affirmed, “Oh, definitely, yes. Secretary Rubio will be meeting Minister Jaishankar, and I think they will be talking not only about bilateral issues, of course, including US-India relations, but also regional issues, definitely, including the war in West Asia, the Ukraine-Russia war and overall global affairs.”

US approach increasingly emphasises corporate deals, says expert

Analysing overarching trends in Washington’s foreign policy approach, he concluded, “But it indicates to me one other thing in regard to American policy. It seems that America is now adopting a stance or a position of engaging with India in terms of corporate deals.

The strategic component is there, no doubt, and a strategic partnership is there, as Minister Jaishankar also says, but to me, it seems that America is emphasising more on business and corporate deals with India and understanding that the trade deal, for example, and the strategic partnership, for that matter, are separate buckets which can be handled separately or together, but their first emphasis is on large business deals with India.”

Jaishankar to host Rubio and UAE foreign minister in Mumbai

Adding official context to these diplomatic movements, External Affairs Minister (EAM) S Jaishankar will host counterparts from the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and the United States (US) in Mumbai on October 19-20, while also attending celebrations marking the 250th anniversary of US independence as a Guest of Honour, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) stated on Friday.

Responding to a question from ANI during a bi-weekly media briefing in New Delhi, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal stated that the meeting between EAM Jaishankar and his UAE counterpart, Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, would provide an opportunity to review all dimensions of bilateral cooperation, alongside discussions on the situation in West Asia, as well as global and multilateral matters.

Elaborating on the schedule, Jaiswal stated, when asked about EAM Jaishankar’s upcoming meetings, “On October 19 and 20, 2026, the External Affairs Minister will host in Mumbai the Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of the UAE, His Highness Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, for an official visit. On October 20, the External Affairs Minister will hold talks with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and attend the celebration of the 250th anniversary of the independence of the United States of America as the Guest of Honour.”

He further added, “The visit of the UAE Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister will be an opportunity to review all facets of bilateral cooperation under the India-UAE Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. The two delegations will assess and take forward initiatives in the areas of energy, trade, investments, fintech, defence and connectivity. There will naturally be an opportunity also for a detailed exchange on the situation in West Asia, as well as on global and other multilateral issues.”

Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan’s upcoming visit to India follows EAM Jaishankar’s recent official visit to the UAE from October 14-16, during which he held discussions with the country’s leadership and attended the Raisina Middle East event.

India-US talks to cover energy, trade, investment and defence

The MEA spokesperson noted that US Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s forthcoming visit to India would provide an opportunity for both nations to review bilateral ties and explore avenues to further strengthen the Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership.

Jaiswal stated, “In so far as the visit of the Secretary of State is concerned, this forthcoming visit will provide an opportunity for both sides to review India-US relations and discuss ways to further strengthen the Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership that we have with the United States.

Discussions are expected to cover key areas of our bilateral cooperation, including energy, trade, investment, defence, critical emerging technologies and other areas of mutual interest. The two sides will also exchange views on regional and global developments. The visit will provide an opportunity to sustain the high-level engagement between the two countries and advance our shared priorities.”

According to the US State Department, Rubio will travel to Mumbai and Jamnagar next week for talks encompassing “enhanced energy cooperation”. During his visit, Rubio is scheduled to meet senior government officials to consolidate the US-India strategic partnership, share perspectives on regional and global dynamics, and discuss prospects for enhanced energy cooperation. Additionally, the US State Department confirmed that he would interact with business leaders to foster opportunities for commercial investment and economic cooperation.

MEA cites precedent for hosting foreign dignitaries outside Delhi

Addressing queries regarding the selection of Mumbai as the venue for EAM Jaishankar’s bilateral engagements, Jaiswal responded, “It has been the practice for the last decade or so that we have hosted foreign dignitaries outside Delhi.

To just give you some examples, the Prime Minister hosted the Prime Minister of Spain in Baroda. He hosted Chancellor Merz in Ahmedabad. The Prime Minister of Mauritius was hosted by him in Varanasi, and the External Affairs Minister hosted the SCO Foreign Ministers Meeting in Goa.

He hosted the Foreign Minister of Botswana in Kevadia in Gujarat, and the External Affairs Minister also hosted the Heart of Asia Conference in Amritsar. So, that was just to give you a few examples of the meetings of leaders, of dignitaries that have happened outside of Delhi.”

data.title: Violent Protests Rip Through Cities Across France— WSJ
data.description:
By Stacy Meichtry

PARIS — Rioters rampaged through cities across France on Saturday as weeks of student protests broadened to a wider movement of people angry over the rising cost of living.

In Marseille, rioters used a metal barricade to ram through the door of city hall, allowing a crowd of young masked people to storm the building and graffiti its lobby. In Lyon, the city's office of tourism was set ablaze and stores were vandalized. In Paris, rioters torched cars and blocked the streets with burning barricades. Security forces scrambled to reinforce the area around the Élysée Palace and other sensitive sites after protesters sought to converge on government buildings, according to French officials.

The scenes marked a sharp escalation in violence for a protest movement that has strained the country's security forces and political establishment.

The chaos on Saturday erupted amid a nationwide protest over the cost of living that drew tens of thousands of people of all ages onto the streets, ranging from high-school students to some of the country's most prominent left-wing politicians. Jean-Luc Mélenchon, the far-left firebrand who is rising in polls ahead of next spring's presidential election, spearheaded one group of protesters marching in Paris.

Lyon Mayor Grégory Doucet said rioters armed with Molotov cocktails were operating "in parallel" with peaceful protesters, stretching police forces.

"The situation is really disorienting," he said.

Protesters are demanding the government take costly measures to boost consumers' purchasing power and invest in the education system. Their demands, however, are colliding with the financial realities of a cash-strapped French state.

Investors have pushed France's borrowing costs to some of their highest levels in decades amid concerns the country's political class is incapable of reining in public spending that has resulted in years of budget deficits above 5% of gross domestic product.

In a bid to reassure markets, the government has proposed EUR43 billion, equivalent to $49 billion, in spending cuts for its 2027 budget. The proposed cuts, however, have deepened public anger and fueled the protests.

"To those who clearly want to use these acts of violence as a 'warm-up' before the presidential election, I say this plainly: we will not be intimidated," Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said Saturday, adding: "Public money is scarce: it must fund our public services, not endlessly repair what vandals destroy.

The protests began last month with blockades at high schools as students demanded more teachers, smaller classes and greater investment in dilapidated school buildings. On Saturday the protests spread to trade unions and members of the yellow-vest protest movement that began in 2018 over fuel prices — becoming a locus of broader discontent over the state of France's public services.

The government has mobilized thousands of police in a bid to contain the violence. Clashes with police in previous protests, however, have resulted in gruesome injuries to minors, exacerbating tensions and fueling turnout at subsequent demonstrations. One teenager's hand was blown off by a dispersal grenade, another lost an eye, while a 14-year-old boy suffered a jaw fracture.

"I've attended protests since I was a kid, and I've never seen anything like what's going on in Paris right now," Sandrine Rousseau, a green party lawmaker, told French TV.

As the protests have gathered force, the French electorate has become increasingly polarized. Polls show public support is rising for far-right leader Marine Le Pen, the front-runner in next year's presidential election. Mélenchon, the far-left leader, has emerged as her main rival while support has stalled for candidates who once governed under Macron.

"The French people, who can no longer bear being caught between the austerity and fiscal hammering of those in power and the insurrectionary activists, must hold out for a few more months," Le Pen wrote on X.

data.title: CIA deputy director says Bitcoin is a tool for intelligence collection
data.description:
Bitcoin was sold to many early adopters as digital cash that nobody could trace. The CIA's second-in-command would like a word.

CIA Deputy Director Michael Ellis said in a May 1, 2025 podcast interview that Bitcoin is not truly anonymous, and that US intelligence uses it to collect information on adversaries. For anyone still treating the network as a privacy cloak, that is an awkward thing to hear from a spy agency.

Ellis described Bitcoin as "pseudonymous" rather than anonymous. The difference matters more than it sounds.

On Bitcoin, activity is tied to addresses rather than legal names. Ellis's point is that the gap between an address and a real person can be closed, and authorities are working to close it.

According to Ellis, that gap is what lets US authorities follow illicit activity connected to adversaries. He named drug cartels and terrorist organizations as examples of the groups whose crypto use can be tracked.

"We can disrupt our adversaries' use of it and we can use these technologies to collect more intelligence."

That one sentence covers two separate jobs. One is defensive: interfering with how hostile groups move money. The other is offensive: treating the transactions themselves as a source of intelligence.

Ellis also placed Bitcoin inside a broader technology competition with countries like China. In his framing, crypto is one more front in a contest over which nations master emerging tech.

He also pointed to growing institutional adoption and offered a blunt assessment: "Bitcoin is here to stay."

Ellis was sworn in as CIA Deputy Director on February 10, 2025. His podcast remarks came less than three months into the job.

The views are not new inside the intelligence community. Former Acting CIA Director Michael Morell praised blockchain analytics tools like Chainalysis in a 2021 analysis, crediting them with helping efforts against illicit finance.

The CIA also works with law enforcement to trace illicit payments made with digital assets. Ellis's comments put a more public face on that cooperation.

Blockchain analytics firms essentially do pattern recognition at scale. They cluster addresses, map flows between them, and flag links to known entities, turning a stream of pseudonymous transactions into something closer to a readable map.

The most direct implication is for privacy expectations. Anyone who assumed Bitcoin transactions were invisible to governments now has a CIA official stating plainly that they are not.

For bad actors, the message is sharper. A senior official is publicly signaling that the agency treats their transactions as an intelligence feed.

The CIA's framing of Bitcoin as a national security tool may lift institutional confidence and potentially strengthen its standing with the public and regulators. An asset the intelligence community expects to persist, and is actively building capabilities around, is harder to dismiss as a passing fad.

The China framing deserves attention too. Once a technology gets folded into great-power competition, policy around it tends to be shaped by security priorities as much as by financial regulators.

The practical takeaway for market participants is to separate two questions that often get blurred. Whether Bitcoin is here to stay, as Ellis put it, is one question, and whether using it is private is another, and the CIA's answer to the second is clearly no.

Addressing broader diplomatic schedules and regional discussions, Sachdev affirmed, "Oh, definitely, yes. Secretary Rubio will be meeting Minister Jaishankar, and I think they will be talking not only about bilateral issues, of course, including US-India relations, but also regional issues, definitely, including the war in West Asia, the Ukraine-Russia war and overall global affairs."

Analysing overarching trends in Washington's foreign policy approach, he concluded, "But it indicates to me one other thing in regard to American policy. It seems that America is now adopting a stance or a position of engaging with India in terms of corporate deals.

The strategic component is there, no doubt, and a strategic partnership is there, as Minister Jaishankar also says, but to me, it seems that America is emphasising more on business and corporate deals with India and understanding that the trade deal, for example, and the strategic partnership, for that matter, are separate buckets which can be handled separately or together, but their first emphasis is on large business deals with India."

Adding official context to these diplomatic movements, External Affairs Minister (EAM) S Jaishankar will host counterparts from the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and the United States (US) in Mumbai on October 19-20, while also attending celebrations marking the 250th anniversary of US independence as a Guest of Honour, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) stated on Friday.

Responding to a question from ANI during a bi-weekly media briefing in New Delhi, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal stated that the meeting between EAM Jaishankar and his UAE counterpart, Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, would provide an opportunity to review all dimensions of bilateral cooperation, alongside discussions on the situation in West Asia, as well as global and multilateral matters.

Elaborating on the schedule, Jaiswal stated, when asked about EAM Jaishankar's upcoming meetings, "On October 19 and 20, 2026, the External Affairs Minister will host in Mumbai the Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister of the UAE, His Highness Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, for an official visit. On October 20, the External Affairs Minister will hold talks with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and attend the celebration of the 250th anniversary of the independence of the United States of America as the Guest of Honour."

He further added, "The visit of the UAE Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister will be an opportunity to review all facets of bilateral cooperation under the India-UAE Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. The two delegations will assess and take forward initiatives in the areas of energy, trade, investments, fintech, defence and connectivity. There will naturally be an opportunity also for a detailed exchange on the situation in West Asia, as well as on global and other multilateral issues."

Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan's upcoming visit to India follows EAM Jaishankar's recent official visit to the UAE from October 14-16, during which he held discussions with the country's leadership and attended the Raisina Middle East event.

The MEA spokesperson noted that US Secretary of State Marco Rubio's forthcoming visit to India would provide an opportunity for both nations to review bilateral ties and explore avenues to further strengthen the Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership.

Jaiswal stated, "In so far as the visit of the Secretary of State is concerned, this forthcoming visit will provide an opportunity for both sides to review India-US relations and discuss ways to further strengthen the Comprehensive Global Strategic Partnership that we have with the United States.

Discussions are expected to cover key areas of our bilateral cooperation, including energy, trade, investment, defence, critical emerging technologies and other areas of mutual interest. The two sides will also exchange views on regional and global developments. The visit will provide an opportunity to sustain the high-level engagement between the two countries and advance our shared priorities."

According to the US State Department, Rubio will travel to Mumbai and Jamnagar next week for talks encompassing "enhanced energy cooperation". During his visit, Rubio is scheduled to meet senior government officials to consolidate the US-India strategic partnership, share perspectives on regional and global dynamics, and discuss prospects for enhanced energy cooperation. Additionally, the US State Department confirmed that he would interact with business leaders to foster opportunities for commercial investment and economic cooperation.

Addressing queries regarding the selection of Mumbai as the venue for EAM Jaishankar's bilateral engagements, Jaiswal responded, "It has been the practice for the last decade or so that we have hosted foreign dignitaries outside Delhi.

To just give you some examples, the Prime Minister hosted the Prime Minister of Spain in Baroda. He hosted Chancellor Merz in Ahmedabad. The Prime Minister of Mauritius was hosted by him in Varanasi, and the External Affairs Minister hosted the SCO Foreign Ministers Meeting in Goa.

He hosted the Foreign Minister of Botswana in Kevadia in Gujarat, and the External Affairs Minister also hosted the Heart of Asia Conference in Amritsar. So, that was just to give you a few examples of the meetings of leaders, of dignitaries that have happened outside of Delhi."

data.title: Binance.US Seeks $100 Million Funding Round At $1 Billion Valuation
data.description:
TL;DR: Binance.US is reportedly seeking up to $100 million from private investors at a proposed valuation of approximately $1 billion. The financing discussions come as the American exchange attempts to rebuild after several difficult years.

Binance.US is reportedly pursuing a $100 million fundraising round as it seeks to strengthen its presence in the American cryptocurrency market.

Bloomberg reported on October 15 that the exchange was discussing an investment at a valuation of approximately $1 billion. If completed on those terms, it would represent a sharp reduction from the $4.5 billion valuation attached to its 2022 funding round.

The discussions have not been announced as a closed transaction, and the proposed figures could change.

Rebuilding A Damaged Business

Binance.US once competed aggressively for American cryptocurrency traders but faced major regulatory and operational difficulties.

The Securities and Exchange Commission’s earlier proceedings complicated the company’s relationships with banks and other commercial partners. As NewsBTC covered at the time, those disputes included an emergency application involving assets connected to the platform.

Conditions have since changed, with US regulators adopting a different approach to digital asset businesses. But a friendlier environment alone does not guarantee that customers return.

Fresh funding could support compliance, technology development and new products, while giving Binance.US greater flexibility to compete with established exchanges and brokerages.

What The Valuation Suggests

A proposed $1 billion valuation is not itself a completed market transaction, but it is a reminder of how substantially expectations for cryptocurrency platforms have evolved since 2022.

The next challenge for Binance.US will be demonstrating that investment capital can translate into stronger trading activity and sustainable growth.

For now, the fundraising discussions show renewed ambition rather than a finished recovery.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

data.title: HDFC Bank CEO-designate Bagchi to meet customers, regulators before taking over
data.description:
Mumbai, Oct. 17 -- After joining HDFC Bank, India's largest private-sector lender, as an additional director and chief executive designate, Anup Bagchi said on Saturday that his first priority was to meet customers and regulators.

Bagchi, who is set to take over the reins of the bank on 27 October, said he had been at the bank for "a few days" and knows "many of the teams". He said he would engage with regulators, customers, and stakeholders and gather insights, which would become key inputs for the organization.

Bagchi, who joined from the ICICI Group, was full of praise for the bank and its team. "Exceptional team, very strong team, very able team, and it's a very process-driven institution," said Bagchi. "(I am) thankful to the board for giving me this opportunity. I will work alongside the team and make sure that it goes from strength to strength."

The September quarter was also the last full quarter for incumbent CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan, who rose through the ranks to become chief financial officer in 2008 and then CEO in 2020, after Aditya Puri stepped down.

Bagchi described outgoing HDFC Bank executives Jagdishan and Kaizad Bharucha as "very warm" and said he was going to seek their inputs. He described HDFC Bank as an institution that is not dependent on just one, two, or three individuals.

Bharucha, the bank's deputy managing director, had requested that the board allow him to step down on 31 December, a request the board has accepted, the bank said in a regulatory filing on Saturday.

Long-time insider Bharucha was among the contenders for the top job, but his elevation was constrained by Reserve Bank of India (RBI) regulations that limit the tenure of whole-time directors to 15 years. Bharucha joined the bank's board in 2014, leaving him only until 2029 to remain a director.

Meanwhile, Jagdishan said that Bagchi would lead a team of able leaders who had been with the institution for a long time. "Anup has about 24 years of experience in the field of financial services. He is a seasoned player who has worked not only in banking but also in insurance. So he has a very holistic view," said Jagdishan.

HDFC Bank on Saturday reported a net profit of Rs.19,510 crore for the three months through September, up 4.7% year-on -year. Its other income dropped 3.6% from the year-ago quarter to Rs.13,830 crore.

The bank's net interest margin compressed 10 basis points to 3.16% from the previous quarter and the same quarter last fiscal year. Jagdishan said going forward, with the upward trajectory of interest rates, there should be a change because a large part of its balance sheet is linked to variable benchmarks and therefore there will be a slightly faster transmission on the asset side.

The bank's loan book grew 15.3% on-year to Rs.33 trillion, while deposits grew 18.8% to Rs.33.2 trillion in the same period.

Analysts were underwhelmed. "The weak earnings growth trend for HDFC Bank continued in Q2 FY27," analysts at Bernstein said in a note on Saturday.

Bernstein said that while balance-sheet growth remained healthy and asset quality stayed resilient, weaker treasury income and margin pressure weighed on profitability.

The note pointed out that loan growth continued to be driven by the corporate (16%) and mid-market (24%) segments, reflecting broader industry trends, while retail loan growth remained relatively subdued at 12%.

data.title: When stock valuations go wrong, blame taxes?
data.description:
Those were the days. On September 26, 2024, the Sensex closed at an all-time high of 85,836.12 points. Multibaggers were everywhere, compounders were fashionable, and valuations were an inconvenience best left to old-fashioned investors. Two years later, benchmark indices are down about 13 per cent, with individual stocks suffering far greater damage, including corrections of 50-60 per cent.

Six out of 10 BSE 500 stocks have delivered no positive returns since September 2024, while nearly 7 out of 10 have failed to beat bank fixed deposits. Evidently, the much-celebrated power of compounding has been taking a rather extended holiday. But a new explanation for this disappointment is gaining currency. The problem, apparently, is taxation.

Ahead of the Union Budget consultation process, sections of the market intensified demands for relief from Securities Transaction Tax (STT) and Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) tax. The clamour peaked on October 13 when Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman expressed her willingness to hear the debate, even though she didn’t promise any change. Markets nevertheless found reason to celebrate, gaining 3.5 per cent in the next few sessions.  Even an invitation to debate taxation is apparently worth a rally.

Forgotten wisdom 

Benjamin Graham, the father of value investing, warned nearly a century ago against believing that good stocks remained sound investments regardless of price, calling it a rationalisation of speculative excess.

Had Graham visited Dalal Street in September 2024, he would have found material for another ‘Security Analysis’. The Nifty 50 traded at about 24 times earnings (NSE), while its constituents averaged a staggering 44 times, as per Capitaline.

Consider the stock-specific valuations investors enthusiastically accepted. Trent commanded around 221 times earnings, Tata Consumer Products 90 times, Nestlé India 82 times, Britannia 68 times and Asian Paints 62 times, according to Capitaline.

What extraordinary wealth have these extraordinary valuations created since? Trent is down 43 per cent, Britannia 24 per cent, Asian Paints 29 per cent, Tata Consumer 19 per cent and Nestle India 8 per cent. The businesses did not suddenly become worthless. Investors had paid prices leaving little room for slower growth.

The celebrated IT industry offered another example. IT giants TCS, Infosys and Wipro traded at 25-33 times earnings, growth valuations difficult to reconcile with their maturity and emerging AI disruption. Their sharply negative 32-43 per cent returns underline the danger of assigning growth multiples to mature businesses. Excessive valuations can also reduce pressure on managements to innovate. When investors reward the status quo with premium multiples, dividends and buybacks become easier responses than difficult investments in innovation.

Expensive everywhere 

The problem extended beyond large-caps. In September 2024, the Nifty 500 traded at 28 times earnings, Nifty Smallcap 250 at 32 times and Nifty Midcap 150 at an extraordinary 45 times. Two years later, the latter two indices are down 4 and 3 per cent, respectively.

The relationship between starting valuations and subsequent returns is revealing. The set of stocks trading above 28 times earnings in September 2024 have delivered an average return of just 3 per cent in the ensuing period. Those below that threshold have gained 13 per cent on average.

The biggest casualties include PB Fintech, Sobha, Inox Wind, Adani Green, Kaynes, Jubilant FoodWorks, Voltas, D-Mart, Thermax, Whirlpool India, Havells, Varun Beverages and Godrej Properties. Their P/Es ranged from 80 to 741 times in September 2024, preceding declines of 31-72 per cent.

Of course, valuations alone cannot explain every subsequent decline. Earnings disappointments, business conditions and shifting investor expectations also matter. But paying extravagant prices leaves precious little room for any of these to go wrong.

Convenient scapegoat 

Until recently, India was apparently losing out because it lacked a compelling artificial intelligence (AI) story. Now, taxation has emerged as the explanation for foreign selling. Between September 26, 2024 and October 15, 2026, FIIs sold a net ₹5.7 lakh crore ($63 billion) across 496 sessions, averaging ₹1,150 crore daily. Mind you this coincided with shifting US yields, a firmer dollar and global rotation trades.

But were these foreign investors always so allergic to Indian taxes? FIIs invested ₹1.77 lakh crore in equities in calendar 2023 and ₹2.08 lakh crore in FY24, when global interest rates were still cheap and liquidity in flow. Even after the LTCG rate rose from 10 to 12.5 per cent in July 2024, they invested another ₹61,471 crore in equities during August and September. Apparently, the same taxes that were perfectly tolerable during a bull market became unbearable when valuations stopped making sense.

India’s 12.5 per cent headline LTCG rate on qualifying listed equities is also hardly extraordinary internationally. In the US, combined federal, state and local capital gains taxation can exceed 35 per cent for wealthy investors in high-tax jurisdictions.

Even as foreign capital went elsewhere, relentless domestic SIP inflows have somewhat absorbed the deluge, effectively funding the exit of offshore funds at elevated multiples while retail investors have indirectly funded the ‘Atmanirbhar market’ dream.

None of this means equity taxes are irrelevant. STT raises transaction costs and LTCG tax reduces returns. But the 2019 corporate tax cuts, intended partly to encourage investment, did not immediately unleash the much-awaited private capex boom. Yes, tax concessions can improve profitability and investment incentives, but they cannot create demand or attractive business opportunities. So, there is little reason to assume that reducing stock market taxes will somehow produce better corporate earnings or justify excessive valuations.

data.title: Jio Platforms IPO: Terrific history, but is the future prized or pricey?
data.description:
India’s largest IPO deserves more attention, and this is not just for its size, but the impact Jio Platforms has had on the digital ecosystem in India. The ‘LTE’ or the ‘long term evolution’ of the Indian mobile telephone market has had many inflexion points and few very notable days, but arguably none as significant as the one on September 1, 2016.

As Mukesh Ambani started the 2016 AGM of Reliance Industries (RIL) with announcement of the launch of Reliance Jio’s mobile service, markets started taking note. Over the next one hour as he spoke on the founding vision of Jio to be a key enabler of the digital ecosystem in India and its plans, competitor stocks got crushed (Airtel fell 6.3 per cent, Idea fell 10.5 per cent and it dint end on day one). The banger of a launch had many game-changing announcements.

Likening data to digital life as what oxygen is to life, something that should never be in short supply and unaffordable to any user, he unveiled plans that under cut competitors pricing massively and also brought in whole lot of simplicity in pricing of products. Till then recharging a phone was sometimes a complicated exercise with myriad plans for different use cases with footnotes and caveats for each plan, and there were times when even the highly intelligent would have their head go in a tizzy trying to parse through mobile recharge plans of the various service providers operating then. Jio brought in unbridled simplicity and also announced users would be charged only for data – voice and messaging will be free and unlimited.

This moment was six years in the making and the first steps for a giant leap were taken when Reliance Industries had announced acquisition of a 95 per cent stake in Infotel Broadband in June 2010, and this was just after Infotel Broadband had acquired pan Indian broadband spectrum in the auctions that had closed just a few days earlier.

As compared to competitors upgrading their 2G and 3G networks gradually with different architecture for voice calls/sms and internet, Reliance focused on building a pan India VOLTE or Voice over LTE (LTE stands for long term evolution) – a pure IP network for handling internet/data traffic where even voice is also treated as data. Apparently it was the largest ‘only 4G LTE’ network in the world at the time of launch.

The moment was coming, but nobody expected the extent of disruption that played out. For customers it was a boon (cost per GB of data fell from around ₹228 in FY16 to ₹8 by FY 19), for competitors it was a nightmare. Reliance Communication (Anil Ambani owned telecom player) and Maxis owned Aircel folded up after a failed merger attempt, while Idea and Vodafone India had a successful merger but were driven to the brink of bankruptcy (As AGR liabilities added fuel to fire) before managing to survive.

Industry leader – Airtel showed resilience and came out stronger as it had during previous crisis trying moments in the industry. It had also successfully acquired two other players that struggled after the Jio launch – Tata Docomo and Telenor India. From multiple players, the telecom market shrank to four players – although this is not unusual given globally most large economies have only 3-5 players in the sector.

What Jio did was unparalleled - no where in the telecom world has a player entered the business so late and became number one player (by subscriber count) in a country, that too in such a short time (Jio became the top player in July 2019 – less than 3 years after launch). The top 3 mobile players in major countries across the world – USA, Canada, UK, France, China, Brazil, Mexico, etc, have remained entrenched for over decades.

The best instances of progress for companies in other countries was like T-Mobile in US overtaking Sprint (prior to its merger with Sprint)) to become the third largest player from a distant fourth position (T-Mobile is now the 2md largest player in the US after merger with Sprint). Nowhere was the applecart upset as in India where only one private company – Bharti Airtel managed to survive in the industry in its original form.

Today the per-capital mobile data consumption in India at 26.7 GB a month is the highest in the world and way ahead of countries like US or China where the number is at around 18-19 GB a month. In FY16 prior to Jio entry, per capita number in India was at less than 0.2GB

A terrific history for Jio and the Indian telecom sector. While shareholders of Reliance Industries (RIL) which owns 66.43 in Jio Platforms have benefited (in the five years after launch of Jio – RIL shares were up over 4x, the recent years underperformance notwithstanding), how prized or pricey is the IPO for new investors? Lets dive in!

Pricing and valuation

The IPO of Jio Platforms (Jio) consists of an entirely fresh issue (proceeds go into the company, not existing shareholders) of 27 crore shares at a price band of ₹1,065 to ₹1,119. At the upper end of the band, the company will raise ₹30,213 crore. Company intends to use the proceeds for repayment of borrowings and general corporate purposes.

At the upper end of the price band, the pre-issue and post issue market capitalization of the company will be, 10 lakh and 10.3 lakh crore respectively, which will make it the fourth largest listed company in India by market capitalization after RIL, HDFC Bank and Bharti Airtel (ranking based on their current market capitalization).

Jio’s pre-issue and post issue PE multiple on trailing twelve month basis will be at around – 32.5 and 33.5 times respectively

On an enterprise value (EV) basis ie. market capitalization plus net debt ( including deferred payment liabilities for spectrum), Jio is valued at around 11.14 lakh crore. Here it needs to be understood that on a pre and post issue basis, the EV of the company does not change as the increase in market cap post issue by ₹30,213 crore is offset by a decrease in net debt from similar inflow of cash into the company. On an EV/EBITDA basis Jio is valued at an EV/EBITDA of around 14.4 times (for why EV and EV/EBITDA matter, refer section on Jio vs peers.

Business

Jio’s primary business is executed through its 100 per cent subsidiary – Reliance Jio Infocom Limited (RJIL) which serves 533.3 million customers in India as of June 30, 2016. The services offered encompass – mobile and fixed broadband services to consumers and enterprises.

Other digital services (entertainment suite, cloud services, IoT etc) are offered through other subsidiaries of Jio. In FY26, RJIL accounted for 88 percent of Jio’s revenue and more importantly 95 per cent of its EBITDA and 94 per cent of its PAT. Within these mobile and fixed broadband services business accounted for around 85 per cent of Jio’s revenue and 98 per cent of RJIL’s revenue.

While RJIL does not split its revenue segments between mobile and fixed broadband services, how much is driven by mobile services can be gauged from data provided by its close peer – Airtel. Out of Airtel’s total wireless and fixed broadband services revenue in India, its mobile services revenue accounts for around 78 per cent.

Based on this, investors need to approach Jio with one clear perspective – Jio is and will remain for the foreseeable future a company whose fortunes will depend primarily on the evolution of its mobile services business and to lesser extent on the fixed broadband business. While IPO prospectus refers to company’s primary business as that of a technology platform with a business model built on in-built proprietary technology stack (layered software used to build aps that underlie the telecom network and digital services) and potential to monetize its in-built technology stack via selling it to other telecom service providers globally, for now this has to be treated only as work in progress with limited clarity on financial implications for the same.

As of June 30, Jio’s pan-India mobile digital connectivity network reach extended to more than 99 per cent of India’s population. In FY26, around 60 per cent of India’s wireless traffic was on the Jio’s network. As of June 30, Jio had a total customer base of 53.3 crore, out of which around 50.5 crores or 95 per cent is mobile phone subscribers and rest fixed broadband.

This represents a wireless service market share of around 40 per cent for Jio in India. Jio had 1.4 time 4G/5G subscribers as compared to Airtel. However Jio ‘s average revenue per user (per month) or ARPU at around ₹215 is lower than that of Airtel’s India mobile ARPU of ₹264. Pls note here that unlike Airtel, Jio provides a blended ARPU for mobile and fixed services combined. So based on reasonable assumptions, it is possible that Jio’s mobile ARPU could be around 5 per cent lower than the reported blended ARPU of ₹215.

Jio vs Peers

With business and prospects on one side, it is also important to gain a perspective on how Jio fares vs its immediate peer – Airtel and also other large telecom players globally. In this context it is important to understand why enterprise value and EV/EBITDA are important metrics to assess for telecom players along with PE multiples.

EV refers to the total value of a company. While a company belongs to its equity shareholders, whatever claim they have in the value of a business is only after paying/providing for third party liabilities (bank/bond holders) – primarily the net debt (total debt minus cash/bank balances). In other words, the total value of a company, as perceived by the market, is the sum of its market cap plus net debt.

Also what works in the case of EV is that it helps in doing a capital-agnostic analysis of a company. Whether a company is funded only with equity, or a combination of equity and debt, the total value of the business is the same. Sources of funding don’t matter. By measuring EBITDA (which is before interest payments) and EBITDA margins, a pure operational evaluation and comparison of businesses’ performance can be done (ie PAT and earnings will be impacted by capital structure or debt/equity ratio which is not related to business operations). Specifically in telecom sector EV, EBITDA and EV/EBITDA multiples is widely used, even more that PE multiples as it is usually a capex heavy business and involves debt for most companies. Measuring the band of EV/EBITDA multiples globally can help to for a perspective on valuation too. So here is a comparison.

From these charts, it can be inferred that Jio and Airtel are amongst the most expensively valued telecom companies globally. At the same time, they also have superior EBITDA margins, and better growth rates.

Risk vs Reward

Jio offers access to a well-established and well-managed company with a strong track record. With passive infrastructure (telecom towers, long haul fiber network or dumb pipes) hived off its balance sheet to other group companies, Jio has a relatively lean telecom and digital focused business with only active network assets/capex (radio access networks, switches and routers, landing gateway stations etc) on its books.

While Airtel too has hived of passive infrastructure business, given its majority ownership of Indus Towers, it forms part of its consolidated operations. Its financials have shown consistent growth and performance with stable/improving margins (see chart below), and it also comes with lean clean balance sheet with very minimal debt for a company in the cash guzzling telecom sector. Its cash flow from operations and FCF have also shown consistent improvement over the years.

With mobile broadband penetration (MBB) in India at 68 per cent (MBB customers/total population) as compared to 132 per cent in China and 124 per cent in the US, there is decent scope for the unit numbers to increase for many years further although at a much lower pace than past years. This growth potential is also supported by a future transition to a 5G and 6G world where more and more connected devices get included in the ecosystem.

Telecom business also comes with strong moats and it is hard to disrupt large entrenched players, especially when the entrenched players have a solid balance sheet and fight out any disruptive competition.

So much on the side of reward, but there risks to factor too. At its current pricing Jio is amongst the most expensive telecom services player globally. Given Airtel’s valuation is in the similar range and Airtel’s track record and financials are as solid as that of Jio, unless Jio is materially cheaper vs Airtel, investors will always have to constantly debate which one is better and probably split their investment choices equally between both companies. To an extent Airtel’s premium valuation was driven by lack of good alternative investment options in the telecom sector or what is termed the scarcity premium. With Jio listing, that gets addressed and there is a possibility of valuation margin compression for both companies over the next year.

Finally while ARPU’s in India are extremely low, that does not guarantee a ticket for aggressive pricing increase. While companies in their interest make a case for increase in prices on the pretext that ARPU is low in India, what is of importance to note here is that Indian telecom players also have the most profitable operations globally (see chart). To an extent this will negate the argument for increase in prices as pushed for by companies. Competitive ecosystem will also keep some checks on this.

Balancing out the factors, based on its current valuation Jio is in a zone where it is hard for investors to ignore nor is it extremely attractive. But given its business and potential, it can be considered as a company that can always be part of a well-diversified portfolio with positions added when attractive opportunities are presented. In this context investors must look at the IPO as an opportunity to ‘get a foot in the door’.

data.title: New Scientific Evidence Presented at ANESTHESIOLOGY 2026 Strengthens the Case for Senzime’s TetraGraph and Quantitative Neuromuscular Monitoring
data.description:
UPPSALA, Sweden and SAN DIEGO, Calif., October 17, 2026 — Senzime AB (publ), a global leader in precision-based patient monitoring solutions, today announced new scientific data presented at ANESTHESIOLOGY® 2026, the annual meeting of the American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA). The research highlights important clinical and economic aspects of quantitative neuromuscular monitoring, including the benefits of Senzime's proprietary TetraGraph® technology.

The presentations follow a broad scientific and educational focus on neuromuscular management at this year's congress. More than 25 related sessions, scientific abstracts, quality improvement projects and clinical case presentations address topics ranging from quantitative neuromuscular monitoring and deep-block management to reversal strategies and postoperative outcomes.

“The breadth of neuromuscular management content at this year’s ANESTHESIOLOGY meeting reflects how the science continues to evolve. The conversation is no longer about whether quantitative monitoring should be used, but how it can be used most effectively and integrated into everyday clinical practice,” said Philip Siberg, CEO of Senzime. “We are proud to contribute new scientific evidence addressing two important dimensions of this evolution: helping clinicians gain more meaningful insights during deep neuromuscular block and helping hospitals better understand the clinical and economic benefits of implementing quantitative monitoring.”

TetraGraph's automated deep-block monitoring technology demonstrates substantial improvements in monitoring performance

The study, “Effect of Adaptive Post-Tetanic Count Measurement on Effectiveness of Neuromuscular Monitoring during Deep Block,” analyzed de-identified TetraGraph data from 9,938 surgical cases. The study evaluated TetraGraph's automated, patent-pending deep-block monitoring functionality, Adaptive PTC, and demonstrated substantial improvements in the depth and frequency of neuromuscular block assessment compared with conventional manual PTC activation. The abstract is authored by Sorin J. Brull, MD, FCARCSI (Hon), Julia Nordin, MSc, Jen Sanders, BSN, Linnea Troeng, MSc, Anders Jacobson, MSc, and Ammar Chadaideh, MSc.

New economic model demonstrates potential cost savings from quantitative neuromuscular monitoring

The study, “Cost Concerns of Quantitative Neuromuscular Monitoring—Developing a Return-on-Investment Calculator,”introduces a customizable economic model designed to estimate the potential financial impact of implementing quantitative neuromuscular monitoring.

The model combines published rates of residual neuromuscular block and postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) with reversal drug costs and monitoring expenses to generate institution-specific economic estimates. In a modeled scenario involving 4,000 annual surgical cases requiring neuromuscular blocking agents and an increase in quantitative EMG monitoring adoption from 0% to 90%, the calculator estimated 32 fewer postoperative pulmonary complications annually, approximately $1.23 million in net annual savings after monitoring costs, and a break-even period of approximately 30 days.

These findings illustrate the potential economic value of broader quantitative neuromuscular monitoring adoption, while actual outcomes and savings will depend on individual hospital practices, patient populations and cost structures.

The abstract is authored by Sorin J. Brull, MD, FCARCSI, and Michael J. Noble, MBA. It will be presented on Saturday, October 17, from 10:15 AM to 11:15 AM in the Exhibit Hall, ePosters Monitor 26.

Neuromuscular management takes center stage at ANESTHESIOLOGY 2026

The ANESTHESIOLOGY 2026 scientific program features additional research and education addressing the adoption of quantitative monitoring, comparisons between electromyography (EMG) and acceleromyography (AMG), train-of-four documentation, optimization of reversal strategies, postoperative respiratory and pulmonary outcomes, and clinical cases illustrating the challenges of neuromuscular block management.

Several clinical experts who have collaborated with Senzime are also participating in the scientific program, contributing research and education on contemporary neuromuscular management. Their participation reflects the broader scientific dialogue on how quantitative monitoring can be implemented and optimized in clinical practice. These sessions are independently developed and are not sponsored or directed by Senzime.

data.title: Elon Musk says he should have “focused on AI a little sooner:” Axios

Elon Musk says that he should have “focused on AI a little sooner," cutting short his stint at the White House last year, Axios reported on Saturday, citing a recent interview biographer Walter Isaacson conducted with the Tesla CEO.

Following a public spat with President Donald Trump, Musk formally left the administration in May 2025 after a 130-day tenure spearheading the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), which was involved in thousands of federal job cuts.

His business empire suffered as a result, with Tesla sales falling 13% during the first three months of 2025 as his political affiliations sparked a widespread public backlash against the billionaire investor throughout last year.

I "kinda got carried away, basically," Musk told Isaacson for a new podcast series, "The Builders with Walter Isaacson," premiering on Tuesday. He added that he ended up being "gone for too long" from his businesses.

"What I should have done," he said, "was be more in the background ... and probably only had it last for a month or two,” said Musk, who also leads the newly IPO’d rocket, satellite, and AI company SpaceX .

"I should have gone back and focused on AI a little sooner than I did." He added. Musk also commented on the U.S. budget deficit, which he had previously said would increase because of Trump's "Big, Beautiful Bill.”

There's "no way we were gonna solve the deficit from within the government," Musk said, adding, "The only way we're going to solve the national debt is with AI and robots."

data.title: Zcash Dips As Hackers Turn To Privacy Token, Winklevoss Says ‘Know Your Customer’ Is Becoming ‘Kill Your Customer’
data.description:
Key points:
  • Zcash fell nearly 5% on Saturday, as on-chain analyst Specter said, “Threat actors are actively using ZEC to move stolen funds.”
  • ZachXBT said “alleged DPRK attackers” had begun shielding about $3.8 million in ZEC stolen in a Bitget exploit.
  • On-chain analyst Specter cited incidents like the CryptoBilis Ledger wallet hack and the Triple-A hack, which reportedly resulted in a $12 million loss.

Zcash (ZEC) fell nearly 5% on Saturday as an on-chain analyst said hackers were moving stolen funds through the privacy token. Those shielded transfers relied on the same privacy that Gemini (GEMI) co-founder Cameron Winklevoss defended, saying that “know your customer is becoming kill your customer.”

“Threat actors are actively using ZEC to move stolen funds,” on-chain analyst Specter wrote on Saturday. These exploits included the Bitget hack, where its security systems had flagged unauthorized transfers from some of its hot wallets. The second theft involved Ledger hardware wallets sold by CryptoBilis, a reseller in Southeast Asia, and the third was the Triple-A hack, a Singapore-based stablecoin payments firm. According to Specter, that loss stood at $12 million.

The on-chain analyst’s comments coincided with a steady decline in ZEC’s price. Over the past month, ZEC slipped more than 17%.

ZEC’s price was trading at $1,167 at the time of writing. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around ZEC remained in the ‘extremely bearish’ zone, while chatter around it stayed at ‘low’ levels over the past day.

‘Kill Your Customer’

Zcash’s privacy features were also the focus of a panel at Token2049 in Singapore, where Gemini co-founder Cameron Winklevoss said that identity checks put users at risk.

“Know your customer is becoming kill your customer,” Winklevoss said during the panel. When a vendor holding customer data gets hacked, he said, criminals learn where people live and how much they hold. “They attack you, kidnap you,” he said. “It’s happening right now. All over Europe, France, in particular.”

Former Coinbase (COIN) CTO Balaji Srinivasan, who shared the stage, made a similar point. “No government should be able to force a collection of something they can’t secure,” he said. He said zero-knowledge proofs should replace document uploads, letting users prove they meet a service’s rules without handing over a passport scan.

Winklevoss framed the issue in constitutional terms. “Encryption is a peaceful, non-violent Second Amendment,” he said. “Privacy is a human right.”

Currency Of Western Individuals

The two investors said they saw Zcash as the private version of Bitcoin (BTC), not its rival. “Cash is centralized, private. Bitcoin, decentralized, public. Zcash, decentralized, private,” Winklevoss said.

Srinivasan said Bitcoin’s public ledger suits large holders. “I believe that Bitcoin becomes a reserve currency of Western institutions,” he said. “Zcash is the currency of Western individuals.”

According to Srinivasan, institutions “need to prove their solvency to many people, but a Western individual doesn’t need to do that.” Winklevoss raised Bitcoin’s pseudonymous creator as a test case. “Would Bitcoin have been launched if Satoshi had to reveal his identity? Maybe not,” he said.

data.title: How small-cap funds shed liquidity risk despite rich valuations
data.description:
A bl.portfolio analysis of liquidity stress data released by the mutual fund industry body AMFI shows that actively managed small-cap mutual funds have reduced their estimated liquidity risk over the past year, despite a sharp rise in valuations.

The Nifty Smallcap 250’s price-to-earnings (PE) ratio rose to 34.45 as of September 30, 2026, from 29.96 a year earlier, indicating richer valuations. However, the category’s average time to liquidate 50 per cent of a portfolio fell to 11.9 days from 17.6 days.

Our analysis suggests that the improvement was driven largely by higher market trading volumes and changes in portfolio composition, including greater exposure to relatively liquid stocks and an increase in the number of holdings.

We analysed AMFI’s liquidity stress-test data for 31 smallcap schemes for September 2025 and September 2026, covering liquidation time for 25 per cent and 50 per cent of portfolios, market-cap allocation, cash holdings, AUM and instrument-wise portfolio composition. Here are the key findings:

Liquidity stress eases

The category’s average time required to liquidate 50 per cent of a portfolio fell to 11.9 days in September 2026 from 17.6 days a year earlier. The time required to liquidate 25 per cent also declined to 6.2 days from nine days.

Of the 31 schemes analysed, 19 recorded an improvement in their 50 per cent liquidation time. Most large schemes saw meaningful improvement. Tata Small Cap reduced its liquidation time from 63 days to 35 days, Quant Small Cap from 71 to 46 days, HDFC Small Cap from 69 to 52 days, SBI Small Cap from 61 to 51 days and Nippon India Small Cap from 43 to 27 days.

Only five schemes saw their liquidation time increase, including Bandhan Small Cap, from 14 to 19 days, and Invesco India Smallcap, from eight to 13 days. Seven schemes reported no change, all of them relatively small schemes.

The improvement was broad-based, particularly among larger schemes, indicating a reduction in estimated liquidity stress even as valuations rose.

Improved trading volumes

One key reason for the improvement was increased trading activity in smallcap stocks. The total traded value of Nifty Smallcap 250 stocks on the NSE rose 24 per cent to ₹31.8 lakh crore during April-September 2026, from ₹25.6 lakh crore during the preceding six months.

This matters because the liquidity stress test estimates the time required to liquidate a portfolio partly on the basis of stocks’ trading volumes. Higher traded volumes mean a given position can theoretically be sold faster, lowering the estimated liquidation time.

Shift towards larger stocks

The share of Nifty 100 stocks in the overall smallcap fund portfolio increased to 22 per cent in September 2026 from 18 per cent a year earlier. These stocks generally have higher trading activity and deeper market liquidity than smaller, less-traded stocks, potentially improving portfolio liquidity.

Seven of the 31 schemes also increased their allocation to midcap stocks. Among them, Quant Small Cap, DSP Small Cap, HDFC Small Cap and Bandhan Small Cap raised their midcap allocation by one to seven percentage points.

However, the trend was not uniform. Axis Small Cap, SBI Small Cap and Nippon India Small Cap increased their smallcap allocation by three to eight percentage points while reducing midcap exposure.

Changes in top-10 holdings

Eighteen of the 31 schemes increased their allocation to their top 10 holdings, while 13 reduced it. The trend was mixed across fund sizes. A higher allocation to the top holdings can support liquidity if these stocks are relatively large and actively traded, enabling fund managers to unwind positions more easily.

More stocks in portfolios

Twenty-two of the 31 schemes increased the number of equity stocks in their portfolios. Bandhan Small Cap added 39 stocks, taking its total to 269 as of September 2026, the highest in the category. JM Small Cap added 27 stocks to reach 88, while Nippon India Small Cap added 21 to reach 256.

A larger number of holdings can reduce dependence on individual stocks and allow funds to spread their positions across more securities. This can reduce the size of individual positions relative to trading volumes and, in turn, lower estimated liquidation times.

What it means for investors

The improvement in liquidity stress is a positive development for smallcap fund investors, particularly as valuations have risen. Higher trading volumes, greater exposure to relatively liquid stocks and broader portfolios have helped reduce the estimated time required to unwind positions.

However, lower stress-test estimates do not guarantee that a fund can exit its holdings quickly during a market-wide sell-off. Liquidity can deteriorate sharply when markets turn volatile and trading volumes dry up.

Investors should therefore view liquidity stress tests as an additional risk indicator, alongside valuations, portfolio concentration, fund size and investment strategy. The bl.portfolio MF Star Ratings can serve as another reference when evaluating funds, but should not be the sole basis for investment decisions.
